stories.notes: Cross-platform feature (GO, UP, MX) with empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. openspec must elaborate AC, propose platform splits, and add technical depth for live preview architecture. speckit then hardens with testability criteria, edge cases (real-time sync, preview state isolation, performance), and security checks. Priority high due to complexity and absent AC.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. Derived measurable ACs from the description's concrete deliverable ('editor modifies content → preview reflects changes without full page reload'). Attachment points are useContent (236-caller funnel), ContentstackContext (provider), and contentstack.ts (service layer). VCs stop at the Contentstack boundary (mocked client) per unreachable-service rules.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all 15 criteria are newly derived from the story title/description ('Live Preview of Content in CMS — editor modifies content → preview reflects changes without full page reload'). Openspec's notes identified attachment points (useContent, ContentstackContext, contentstack.ts) and the Contentstack boundary; I kept VCs at that boundary. Key areas covered: (1) core happy path (AC-1), (2) connection lifecycle — open/close/reconnect (AC-2, 3, 5), (3) error handling — network loss, malformed data, timeout (AC-4, 7, 12), (4) edge cases — rapid edits, large payloads, concurrent sessions (AC-6, 11, 14), (5) security — auth, XSS sanitization (AC-8, 9), (6) accessibility — screen-reader live region (AC-10), (7) UX — scroll/focus preservation, toggle (AC-13, 15). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I have not seen the contents of useContent, ContentstackContext, or contentstack.ts. Criteria referencing connection lifecycle, timeouts, and payload handling may need refinement once those implementations are visible. The 2-second and 3-second latency bounds are reasonable starting points but should be validated against real network conditions.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Speckit derived 15 comprehensive ACs covering happy path, connection lifecycle, error handling, edge cases, security, accessibility, and UX — strong coverage. However, openspec under-delivered: it was assigned to elaborate ACs, propose platform splits (GO, UP, MX), and add technical depth, but acceptanceChanged=false and splitCount=0 indicate it produced no concrete ACs and no platform splits. The story title explicitly references three platforms yet no split was proposed, despite coordinator notes requesting it. Both agents show acceptanceChanged=false despite speckit claiming 15 new criteria — this is contradictory and suggests the derived ACs may not have been persisted into the story's acceptanceCriteria array (which remains empty). Speckit's caveat about not having inspected useContent, ContentstackContext, or contentstack.ts means latency bounds (2s/3s) and lifecycle criteria are unvalidated against actual implementation. Human review needed to: (1) confirm whether the 15 ACs were actually written to the story, (2) decide on platform splits or document why a single story is sufficient, (3) validate ACs against real source files.
